messages:
From: John Carter <john.carter@brightcarehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightcarehealth.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: US-state addendum - operator vs service provider & handback scope

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks for the quick call yesterday. Attached is our draft US-state addendum with a few asks we want to confirm before we move to signatures:

1) We want a carveout to allow BrightCare to treat certain telemetry exports as "operator" outputs when used for clinical analytics (we'll call these "BrightCare Insights"). We need clarity that Redwood will not use or monetize those exports for other customers.
2) Handback: if the relationship ends, we require a technical export of onshore telemetry and a 90-day hold for data needed for ongoing patient support. We'd like this reflected as an explicit handback obligation rather than a general deletion clause.
3) Subprocessors: we ask for a 30-day notice period and the ability to object to any subprocessor with a documented business rationale.

Please see attached draft (BrightCare_CCPA_Addendum_DRAFT_v2.docx) and a short redline summary. Can Redwood provide suggested language for a limited-use clause and a practical handback timeline?

Thanks,
John Carter
Director, Legal Ops
BrightCare Health

Attachments: BrightCare_CCPA_Addendum_DRAFT_v2.docx (docx), redline_summary_brightcare.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: US-state addendum - operator vs service provider & handback scope

John —

Appreciate the note and the redlines. High-level responses below; Laura will follow with suggested contract text.

1) Telemetry / "BrightCare Insights": Redwood's standard position for CCPA/CPRA is to act as a "service provider" (limited use) to avoid sale-classification risk. We can add an explicit limited-use clause that: (a) prevents Redwood from using exported telemetry to train models for other customers, and (b) restricts internal analytics to aggregated, de-identified metrics.

2) Handback: a technical export + 90-day retention window is workable in principle but we need to scope which data classes are in-scope (raw request logs, KV cache snapshots, aggregated telemetry). For raw logs we typically provide an export within 30 days, with an optional paid extension for longer holds. We propose: 30-day export for raw logs, 90-day retention for telemetry used for customer support, with a documented handback manifest.

3) Subprocessors: 30-day notice is standard; objection rights are reasonable but must be limited to a narrow set of security/compliance concerns (e.g., HSM provider or data center location). We can't accept blanket vetoes.

I'll let Laura propose redline language and Tessa can comment on operational feasibility for cache snapshots and KV exports.

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Legal & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--

John —

Attached is proposed contract language that aims to balance BrightCare's need for onshore control and Redwood's obligation to avoid uses that would reclassify data as a "sale." Key bullets from the draft redline:

- Limited-use clause: "Redwood shall process Customer Data solely to provide the Services and shall not use Customer Data to develop, improve, or derive models, products, or services for other customers unless Customer gives prior written consent."

- Telemetry exports (BrightCare Insights): "Exports delivered to Customer under the Handback shall be labeled as Customer Outputs. Redwood shall not retain or use such exported Outputs for any marketing, monetization, or model training purposes."

- Handback timeline: "Redwood will provide a full technical export of in-scope datasets within 30 days of a termination request. Redwood will retain support-relevant telemetry for up to 90 days post-termination to enable operational continuity; any extension beyond this period may be provided under a separate retention agreement for an additional fee."

- Subprocessor notice & objection: 30 days' notice; Customer may object only on documented legal/regulatory grounds. If Redwood cannot remediate within 30 days, Customer may either require onshore fallback or terminate the affected service.

I've attached the redline summary and a separate operational note on what we can export from the runtime (for Tessa's review).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

John / Team —

Operational answers from the runtime side:

- KV cache snapshots: by default they contain model-internal keys and transient tokens. We do not store customer PII in KV caches unless a customer explicitly configures prompt-level logging. For BrightCare we can include an explicit opt-in for prompt logging and mark any snapshot containing PII as "export-limited" with an encrypted delivery to your onshore bucket.

- Export manifest: we'll include a per-dataset manifest listing field-level pseudonymization status, retention window, and whether data is encrypted at rest in transit. That should satisfy your security team's ask.

- Subprocessor remediation: 15 days is tight for some infra changes; we can commit to 15 days for enabling onshore fallback when the subprocessor is a transient cache or third-party analytics provider, but require 30 days for major infra providers (data centers, core HSMs). We will include an escalation path to the Redwood Security Director for disputes.

- Audit right: Redwood can offer an annual compliance certificate and remote evidence review (SOC + redacted logs) via a secure portal. Full on-site audits are available under a separate audit addendum.

I'll incorporate these operational notes into Laura's redline and re-send. If that lands, we can ask procurement to circulate an SOW and target sign within 2–3 weeks.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Runtime Operations
Redwood Inference
